newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds shrug off losses after French election.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds shrug off losses after French election.

text.p: Irish bonds recovered much of Monday's losses during moderate late trade on Tuesday with some curve-steepening and investors showing good interest in the short end of the market, dealers said.

"The French election result blurred the EMU picture and hit long end bonds so we're pleased to see some convergence today," a dealer said. "The Irish pound looks a bit more stable so that's helped the market as well."
By 1510 GMT the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up five pence at 102.00 to yield 5.95 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was up 10 pence at 108.70 to yield 6.70 percent.

Dealers said that yields against German bunds had converged by four or five basis points on Tuesday following a divergence of eight points in the five-year area, and four basis points in the 10-year area on Monday.
On Tuesday the yield against Germany was 139 basis points over in the five-year bond, and 76 over in the 10-year.
Irish bonds were marked down on Monday in line with other peripheral markets after a surprise Socialist victory in the first round of the French elections stirred fears about the chances of EMU.

The second round of the French elections takes place on Sunday and there is speculation that the centre-right government will be able to pick up some support from those who abstained in the first round, now that prime minister Alain Juppe has said he will stand down whatever the outcome.
Lionel Jospin, leader of the French socialist party has said he will take no more measures to reduce the budget deficit so that France can qualify for EMU.
"This suggests that could be looking at a softer Euro than we thought or a delayed (monetary) union," a dealer said. "Either way, it's negative for the long end of the market."

Looking ahead, dealers said, the Irish Central Bank's annual report, due later this afternoon, would be scrutinised for hints to inflation and to the bank's attitude on recent foreign exchange turbulence.
Later in the week, U.S. durable orders on Wednesday, and U.S. jobless figures on Thursday would be of interest.
